questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to start a collection of old coins
Famous films about treasure hunters
The illegal trade in ancient objects and how to deal with it
The history of famous museums in London and Paris and their collections
questions.why: They discuss criminal networks that steal and sell ancient artefacts, and what can be done about it.

questions.q: What is the oldest thing Beth has at home?
options: A rocking horse that belonged to her father
Some books from her childhood
A Roman coin she bought in a London shop last year
An old necklace from Turkey
questions.why: Beth says she has a rocking horse that was her dad's.

questions.q: What did the BBC reporter Ryan Keane buy?
options: A small Greek statue
An Egyptian mask
A piece of Roman jewellery from a market
A coin about 1,800 years old
questions.why: Beth mentions the 1,800-year-old Roman coin Ryan recently bought in London.

questions.q: What did Ryan find out while researching other artefacts?
options: Most of the ancient objects sold online are actually fake copies
Some objects sold online and in shops had been stolen
Buying ancient coins is now illegal in the UK
Museums sell their old objects to the public
questions.why: He found reports that some artefacts sold online and in stores had been looted and trafficked.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention colonial times?
options: To show that taking ancient objects is not a new problem
To explain why museums are so popular today
To show that social media started the problem
To praise how carefully ancient objects were protected in the past
questions.why: He says stealing ancient objects is nothing new and artefacts were often taken abroad in colonial times.

questions.q: According to researcher Amr Al-Azm, how has social media changed the trade?
options: It helps the police to find stolen objects much more quickly
It has made buyers more careful
Sellers can now contact buyers directly and easily
It has made ancient objects much cheaper
questions.why: He says sellers used to need intermediaries to reach buyers, but social media 'opens it up'.

questions.q: What did Victoria Reed help her museum do in 2024?
options: Buy a famous Egyptian statue
Open a new gallery of Roman coins
Catch a gang of criminals who were stealing from museums in Boston
Give back a necklace taken from Turkey
questions.why: She helped return an ancient necklace taken illegally from Turkey in the 1970s.

questions.q: What is Victoria Reed's view on returning artefacts?
options: All artefacts should go back to their home countries
She takes a balanced approach and decides carefully
Museums should never return any objects
Only private collectors should return objects
questions.why: She takes a 'middle-of-the-road' approach and believes in 'judicious repatriation decisions'.
